t: In eighteen twenty-two, a musket went off by accident and shot a young fur trader in the stomach.
Army doctor William Beaumont didn't think he'd last the night.
But Alexis St. Martin lived. Only, the wound never closed. It left a hole, straight into his stomach.
Back then, nobody knew how digestion worked. Beaumont saw a window.
He tied meat, bread and cabbage to a silk string, lowered them in, and pulled them out every hour to see what was left.
In a jar, the stomach juice slowly dissolved meat, all by itself.
So the stomach doesn't just grind food. It digests it with acid.
Over two hundred experiments. St. Martin got so fed up, he ran away to Canada. Beaumont brought him back.
He outlived his doctor by almost thirty years. And his family buried him extra deep, so no doctor could take his stomach.
Would you let a doctor look inside you for science? Tell me in the comments.
